task: Task 11 — Nevada Pass-1 sampler A/B at n=5 per arm
verdict: RETIRED, not established. The n=1 attribution is withdrawn.

findings.1_causal_claim_refuted: NV-DOM-03 fails in 5/5 draws of BOTH arms. The n=1 A/B's claim that reverting the sampler reintroduces the two domain-code failures is false for NV-DOM-03 and only partly true for NV-DOM-02 (3/5 in arm A vs 5/5 in arm B). At n=1 arm A drew the 46/46 run the paper already reports as the top of a distribution.
findings.2_what_the_sampler_actually_does: Mean code accuracy 0.965 vs 0.935 — arm A's WORST draw beats arm B's every draw. It eliminates NV-SUB-06 outright (0/5 vs 5/5) and roughly halves NV-DOM-02. It does not touch NV-DOM-03. State it as a rate, not a cause.
findings.3_a_finding_AGAINST_the_sampler: Arm A loses a golden element in 2 of 5 draws (recall 0.978); arm B holds 1.000 in all five and has stdev 0.0 on code accuracy. The layout sampler buys a modest consistent code gain at the cost of run-to-run instability the stride sampler does not have. Not currently in the paper; the sampler must not be described as strictly better.
